The content is mostly other players. Since they can attack you at any time, you always have to take them into account in your decision (are you willing to carry that much gold while being low life? If you do, you risk losing it, if you don't you will lose some of your precious time). If you attack another player, you will be hunted down, but if he's rich you can cash in a lot of gold. Is it worth it?

On top of that, you can create a guild, but unlike most other mmorpg, you can lose it. Mutinies are plots can happen (see here ). You are the guild master, you can take what you want, but if you take too much, they might start a mutiny, if you take too little, they will become stronger than you, plot and betray you. If you only play with your friends in order to prevent that from happening, you will be a small guild with no real hope of getting your hands on the good stuff. Politics are at the core of the game mechanics.

It is not a game about doing things, it is a game about planing and thinking things.

It’s now very confusing for someone like us who do not spent a lot of hours in 2K15’s courts. We do understand that the development team of 2k series likes to tweak controls to optimize the experience, but we still cannot digest these major changes. For e.g., calling off plays with the D-pad is much easy than with the left bumper; in fact, we would have argued with the opposite. Pick-and-roll is also made harder to run, as we now have to merge the right trigger and the left bumper to properly execute the shoots - all around by using the right stick to move our player in the game.
